claims.statement: The DORA register is a binding, structured, multi-template data obligation covering contractual arrangements with ICT third-party providers.
Official evidence establishes significant data-quality pain: only 6.5% of almost 1,000 dry-run registers passed all checks.
Polish entities experienced EBA rejection and a required resubmission stage in 2025.
Official Excel forms, instructions, technical packages, and FAQs are free internal substitutes for entities with capable GRC teams.
An exact Polish incumbent already automates register preparation and validation at EUR 2,000-8,000 per year.
Vendorica and ReportAct further compress differentiation and establish transparent recurring price anchors.
A focused entrant is plausible only if a partner channel and evidence-linked extraction materially outperform incumbent setup and review costs.
Reachable entity count, partner commitment, buyer budget, procurement duration, contract-change frequency, and extraction accuracy remain unknown.
No direct evidence establishes illegality, unobtainable essential rights, mathematically impossible conservative economics, or a non-delegable founder incompatibility.

contrary_evidence: DAPR is a Warsaw-based exact incumbent with a mature register product and transparent EUR 2,000-8,000 annual pricing.
Vendorica already offers AI agreement extraction, live vendor-contract-asset data, continuous reconciliation, and regulatory export.
ReportAct offers another low-entry recurring product, while official KNF and ESA templates remain free.
Dry-run and resubmission pain may decline as entities learn the annual process, so recurring value beyond filing must be proven.
Confidential-contract procurement and security requirements favor established vendors and internal GRC platforms.
